companies.name: Frontier Computing
companies.tagline: Scalable biological brains for ML training substrates.
companies.about: Frontier Computing, founded in 2025 by Michael Domarkas and backed by Y Combinator, operates at the intersection of biotechnology and artificial intelligence. The company is developing scalable biological neural networks to serve as a substrate for machine learning training, addressing the high costs associated with training large parameter count models on traditional hardware. The core of Frontier's offering is a proprietary tissue-culture approach that overcomes the traditional limitations of in-vitro neuron scaling. While academic efforts have generally been confined to approximately 1 million neurons, Frontier has engineered a method to surpass this, with a pathway to scale to over 100 million neurons. This is achieved by solving the vascularization problem, which limits oxygen supply to cells in larger cultures. This technology collocates memory and compute at the substrate level, which enables the training of models with significantly larger parameter counts than what is tractable with conventional GPU architectures. Founder Michael Domarkas, a former Cambridge Natural Scientist, began culturing neuronal tissues with grant funding at the age of 17. His work led to the development of a scalable neuronal culture platform, which he validated by training a biological brain to play the game 'Frogger'. The company was founded in 2018 by Professor Amit Nathwani and is headquartered in London, United Kingdom, stemming from proprietary innovation from University College London (UCL). Professor Nathwani, who also serves as CEO, is an entrepreneur in cancer research and gene therapy and previously founded Freeline Therapeutics. He recognized the limitations of existing medicine, which drove him to create new approaches for patients with unmet needs. NovalGen's core technology is a proprietary autoregulation (AR) platform designed to create safer and more effective drugs by integrating self-regulating capabilities into immunotherapies. This technology aims to mitigate toxicity, improve efficacy, and expand the therapeutic index of treatments like T-cell engagers. The business model focuses on advancing its pipeline of therapeutic candidates through clinical trials, facilitated by a network of academic and strategic partners. The company secures funding from institutional investors, including AlbionVC and UCL Technology Fund, to support its research and development. companies.name: Little Journey
companies.tagline: Little Journey supports children & their families undergoing healthcare procedures or participating in clinical trials
companies.about: Little Journey is a digital eSupport platform designed to psychologically prepare, support and inform children and families before, during and after healthcare interactions - both those occurring as part of a clinical trial and within routine care. Our mission is to support all children to better health. We believe that, through the provision of engaging, interactive and age-appropriate content, we can improve healthcare experiences and health outcomes for all. The Little Journey smartphone app enables families to access information and support tailored to their child’s age, procedure type and hospital at a time and location convenient to them. Virtual tours using 360-degree images of the actual rooms families will visit explain what will happen and who children will meet during their hospital journey. Relaxation animations and therapeutic/distraction games further help to reduce anxiety and improve experiences. A parent information section includes articles, checklists and hospital guides – all of which can be configured by healthcare organisations via a web portal. We ensure a truly patient-focused user experience by co-creating content, using a continuous feedback loop with children, families and key stakeholders. Little Journey fundamentally believes in the power of familiarisation and desensitization through immersive play to facilitate individual coping strategy development, reducing peri-procedural anxiety and improving healthcare experiences for all.

companies.tagline: Community-delivered therapeutic exercise programs for better health and wellbeing
companies.about: Good Boost operates as a social enterprise focused on health technology, transforming community spaces like public swimming pools into therapeutic centers for individuals with musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions. The company was established as a social enterprise in 2018 after originating from a community health research project in Oxford, England. The concept was developed by CEO Ben Wilkins, whose background includes a Master's Degree in Musculoskeletal Science from the University of Oxford and another in Osteopathic Medicine from Oxford Brookes University. Wilkins' motivation stemmed from personal experiences with his mother's arthritis and his own recovery from a snowboarding accident, which highlighted the scarcity of accessible MSK support. His work with charities and social enterprises further revealed the challenges patients faced in staying active before major surgeries like hip and knee replacements. Good Boost's core offering is an AI-powered platform that delivers personalized therapeutic exercise programs for both water and land-based rehabilitation. The technology, a Class 1 Medical Device registered with the MHRA, is built on clinical research and is co-designed with stakeholders to ensure it meets user needs. It creates tailored exercise plans that consider individual conditions and goals, allowing for both solo and group sessions. companies.about: Voy (formerly Manual.co) offers a comprehensive weight loss program that integrates personalised coaching and medication to help individuals achieve sustainable weight loss. The program is designed for those who have struggled with traditional diet and exercise methods, providing a tailored approach that addresses both physical and emotional aspects of eating. Clients begin their journey with an online assessment to determine the most suitable treatment plan, followed by discreet delivery of prescribed medication and regular coaching sessions to track progress and reshape habits. The business primarily serves individuals seeking long-term weight management solutions, leveraging a subscription-based model to generate revenue. By focusing on personalized care and continuous support, Voy aims to enhance client outcomes, with participants reportedly losing five times more weight compared to diet and exercise alone. The program also addresses emotional eating, offering strategies to manage it effectively. companies.name: Epsilogen
companies.tagline: Epsilogen is a global leader in the development of immunoglobulin (IgE) antibodies to treat cancer.
companies.about: Epsilogen is a clinical-stage immuno-oncology company established in 2016 as a spin-out from King's College London. The company was founded by Professor Sophia Karagiannis, a translational cancer immunologist with extensive experience in both academic and biotechnology settings in the USA and UK. Her research group at King's College London was the first to design, evaluate, and advance anti-tumor Immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibodies from a concept into clinical trials. Epsilogen is focused on developing a new class of antibody therapeutics for cancer treatment, leveraging the unique properties of different antibody isotypes, primarily IgE. The company's business model is centered on the research, development, and eventual commercialization of these novel antibody-based drugs. Its revenue generation will depend on achieving clinical milestones, potential partnerships with larger pharmaceutical companies, and ultimately, drug sales upon regulatory approval. Epsilogen has successfully raised significant capital to fund its operations, securing a total of $70.3 million over nine funding rounds. Key investors include Novartis Venture Fund, British Patient Capital, Epidarex Capital, 3B Future Health Fund, and ALSA Ventures. companies.name: Fresh Check
companies.tagline: Visual color-change hygiene verification swab and app
companies.about: Fresh Check Ltd. develops technology to detect bacterial and chemical contamination on surfaces. Founded in London in 2015 by Imperial College London PhD alumni Alex Bond and John Simpson, the company originated from their research into visualizing microbial contamination. The idea was born out of personal frustration with food spoilage and the risks of food poisoning. The company's core offering is the FreshCheck Hygiene Verification System, which consists of a patented color-changing swab and a digital application available on Android and iOS. This system provides a visual, qualitative result in under 30 seconds, indicating whether a surface is clean or contaminated without requiring an expensive reader. The technology is designed to be a simpler and more affordable alternative to traditional ATP (adenosine triphosphate) testing, reducing false positives from sanitizers and non-hazardous food residues. The swabs are stable at room temperature, simplifying storage and reducing waste. Fresh Check serves clients in the food, hospitality, and healthcare industries, including food manufacturers and food service companies. The business model is centered on selling the consumable swabs and providing access to the digital platform for data capture, trend analysis, and reporting. The company has raised a total of $1.3 million in funding over three rounds and was valued at $2.43 million as of July 2021.
